question: What is the buyer feedback on customer service and returns for the Moto G7?

chunks.text: Already submitted feedback to Amazon to check out shipping delays coming out of Houston, as I have never had such delayed -- or "lost" -- shipments before, and two in a row of the same item. Now, I'm awaiting the replacement shipment to arrive, just so I can ship it back. It was a huge mess. Amazon should be thankful I even reported that the first "lost" shipment arrived, that I paid it, and that I will be returning the replacement. I'm sure there are a lot of customers who would've just kept both shipments without saying a word.

Dead in four months. Worked fine for almost four months and now won't boot. The description says this item has a US warranty which should be for one year. However, I can find no way on the Amazon site to return an order I have had for more than a month nor any way to get it repaired under the alleged warranty. Amazon customer service seems to service its' customers in a manner akin to a bull servicing a cow.

Secondly, he did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING to either address or resolve my problems with this phone. He is all lip service for appearance's sake so that Amazon customers will be duped into thinking that Motorola has good customer service. Part of his job apparently is to read Amazon reviews for this phone and answer them with some simple reply in order to mislead customers into thinking he/Motorola might actually try to help them. But, if you actually follow through and submit your Amazon review to him for resolution, he does NOTHING. Don't be fooled into thinking that Motorola cares about customer satisfaction. If you pay for this product and it has manufacturing defects that materialize after the first month or so, you will be out of luck and stuck with this GARBAGE phone. Motorola doesn't care about your satisfaction, only about your initial purchase, so that they get your money.

Buyer Beware!. I have had nothing but issues. The phone shuts off for who knows what reason, Amazon of course closes the return window very quickly - by the time I got the Sim card and Verizon activated the device, I was out of town working and the return window closed. Motorola is replacing the device (supposedly) but I don't have a lot of faith that the replacement is going to be any better than the original. If I could go back I would Pony up and get a Samsung or Apple Phone.

Buyer beware. Phone stopped charging after a year. It didn't fully stop charging, though--the phone can tell something is plugged in--it just charges about 1% per half an hour. Don't think you'll get good customer support or be able to get it fixed for less than $150, either. Not sure if you get a $50 discount for trading in your old phone and its components, or if the $50 discount is for being a customer.

Terrible customer service from motorola.. Had a issue with the phone and motorola support was terrible. Customer agent was very rude and unprofessional and so was her supervisor. I've been buying the motorola series phones for years but no longer. Phones aren't very durable and the support team is terrible.

Buyer beware if you are on a carrier other than the big 4. I like the phone, but I can't connect to to LTE on Ting. Don't buy unless you are on the big 4 networks or don't care about a data connection. I even contacted Motorola via chat about the issue and told to return the phone. No troubleshooting, just return the phone. I like the phone, but the connectivity problems and tech support knock it down to two stars for me.

Bad Phone for US. Camera died in less then 60 days of operation. Seller(Cellmigo) holds to a 30 day return policy, and since the phone is not warrantied in the US Motorola will do nothing for you. Amazon also states that their 90 day A to Z policy won't apply either(it seems useless to even have it in this situation). So buyer beware, you'll be out $300 and stuck with a useless phone. I'm pursuing other avenues to resolve this. I would avoid Cellmigo as a seller as well. If they offered to exchange it for a different phone I would feel otherwise, because they are selling a product with no warranty here(that would make them seem a fair seller to me, but their hands off approach tells me otherwise) I would be suspect of any item sold by them.

I finally called directly, and (after dealing with a surly customer rep) was transferred to the Warranty dept. The customer rep there was very nice, and after reviewing what I had submitted, said it was clearly under warranty. But when she tried to change the status, her system wouldn't let her do it. So she said she had to "escalate" it to the IT department, and assured me I'd hear back in 24-48 hours. Since then, my inquiries have resulted in "IT is working on it" and "they can't seem to verify the IMEI number." I even tried to ask if I could talk directly to IT, but was informed that the Warranty dept was the highest I could go by talking directly. And of course, they always thank me for my patience (ha!) It's now been 6 days and still no answer.

I'm looking in to it and will update my review when I find out what's wrong . I may have to get a replacement after speaking with Amazon customer service, but it will be an insane inconvenience to have to set a new phone up all over again with my provider as well as all my accounts and phone settings which took a week . I can't really say much more until I know where the issue lies , but I've definitely been having issues since I got it . This phone is Tracfone branded . The other one I had , even though it was a demo , was not tracfone. It was just a Motorola phone sold from a Cricket store . I don't know if that is the issue ... if the quality is the same or not because they're sold or branded differently .
